column5: Single-system sound sits 18 frames ahead of its picture, so after a splice the first 18 frames of the new shot carry the old scene's sound (about 1 second at 18 fps, 0.75 s at 24 fps by our arithmetic). Plan the first second of a shot as silent, or transfer to fullcoat for frame-accurate editing
Super 8 cameras of the period offered single-frame exposure and built-in intervalometers for time-lapse, plus existing-light (XL) cameras with fast lenses and special shutters
Chapter II is a 1974-76 hardware survey with prices and models. Dated, so no prices or models are used
8 mm work tends to run high shooting ratios, so the editor takes a larger creative role; the report recommends rough editing single-system and fine cutting double-system

Super 8 stocks were mostly positive reversal, which gives a projection-contrast image directly. Copies add contrast and exaggerate colour, and the report ranks print routes by quality: reversal to positive print, reversal via internegative, then negative to positive print

Editing the camera original is common in 8 mm because workprints cost about as much as the original processing and edge numbers are rarely available. The cost is giving up laboratory fades and dissolves, which have to be done in camera

A 1976 report lists telecine film chain or flying-spot scanner as the two routes from 8 mm film to a television signal, and says Kodak's video player was used mostly to transfer 8 mm film to videotape
The report puts the 16 mm image area at about three times Super 8's, which fills the Super 8 frame-size gap in the gauges table (no millimetre figure is given in the readable text)

Its advice on film against video matches the course's hybrid theme: use video where shooting ratios are very high and power is available, use 8 mm where there is no electricity or equipment may be damaged, and mix both in the edit
All cost tables (kits, per-minute film costs, 1970s dollars) are dated and are not used

Most 8 mm film was positive reversal, which suits shoot, edit and show; extra prints are possible but need foresight in lighting and shoot/edit decisions. Matches the course's description of reversal against negative
